note: The README had grown to 1694 lines -- a reference manual fused with several standalone essays, no longer the human-readable front door a README is for (the 'overwhelm' the branch is named after). Trimmed to ~805 lines: the conceptual spine stays inline (mechanic, category, recipes, rejection, curator, UI, CLI, export/import, serving-a-model's 'it cannot seal', ledger, accuracy), the reference-grade and essay-grade material moved intact into docs/. New files: docs/the-name.md (etymology/Homer/Asimov), docs/accuracy.md (why the numbers are published), docs/project-layout.md (the full annotated manifest), docs/matcher-seam.md (signed embedding cache + tags-and-matcher), docs/frank.md (the fleet forwarder + fleet/home env table), docs/storage-protocol.md (the Storage Protocol reference). tests/test_docs.py updated so the drift gates follow the content to its new home. Draft. Full suite green (the two transient failures were a race with a concurrent dev-deps install, both pass in isolation); ruff + mypy clean; dep-audit fails only on the sandbox's pip/setuptools CVEs.

decisions.question: The README holds too much and reads as a manual. What comes out, and does it get deleted or moved?
decisions.commitment: Moved, never deleted. The material that is reference (the per-file manifest, the Storage Protocol, the Matcher-seam deep dive, FRANK) or standalone essay (the name, why-the-numbers-are-published) is relocated verbatim into its own docs/ file, with a one-line teaser and a link left in the README. The spine -- every concept, the three-state framing, the executed quick-start example, and each recipe's code -- stays inline. Result: 1694 -> ~805 lines, a 52% cut, with nothing lost from the tree.
decisions.why: The README is the one file an outsider reads first; a manual-length one buries the argument it exists to make. But the buried content is not bloat -- IDEAS/TODO record that several long sections were added deliberately over time, and the name/Asimov meditation is loved writing. Deleting it would trade one defect (too long) for a worse one (thrown-away work). Moving preserves every word at an address someone can still find, and the README becomes a door rather than the whole house.
decisions.doors_closed: Deleting the essays to hit a line count (loses crafted work the repo values). Leaving the manifest and protocol reference inline (the two biggest pure-reference blocks, the least front-door content there is).

decisions.question: Two test_docs.py gates required the full module and doc manifest to live inside the README's fenced Project-layout block. Moving the manifest breaks them. Weaken the gates, or move them?
decisions.commitment: Move them. The manifest now lives in docs/project-layout.md; the two gates parse that file instead of the README block, with their assertions byte-for-byte unchanged -- every nestor/*.py and every docs/*.md is still listed, still no ghosts. docs/matcher-seam.md, docs/frank.md and docs/storage-protocol.md join the DOCS scan set for the same reason docs/agent-guide.md already had: they now carry the env-var tables, CLI examples and protocol reference the env/command/flag gates must keep covering.
decisions.why: A drift gate is defined by what it asserts, not where it reads. When content moves, the honest fix is to retarget the gate so it keeps asserting the same thing at the new location -- not to relax it, which would let the manifest drift silently (the exact failure the gate's own docstrings record recurring). Retargeting keeps the coverage total; the gate cannot tell it moved. Registering the new reference docs in DOCS is the same move agent-guide.md got when 263 lines left CLAUDE.md.
decisions.doors_closed: Dropping or loosening the manifest/env gates to make the move pass (silent drift returns). Moving env-var and protocol documentation into docs/ files the gates do not scan (the forward/reverse env gates and the flag gate would stop covering it, undetected).
